thread:
maya: FYI — we want to change the runtime entrypoint for a subset of images to run unprivileged (no root) + privsep helper that pulls secrets from KMS. Need quick sanity check on RBAC, audit logging, and rollback plan before we rebuild base images. :eyes:

alex: Sounds good. Are we doing a sidecar for KMS calls or an init process inside the same container? Sidecar keeps surface smaller, but more infra to manage.

maya: Plan is an init helper in the same image for now (to avoid extra pods), but it will run as a non-root user and escalate only during early boot with a tiny setuid helper that immediately drops privileges. Example snippet: ```ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]
# inside entrypoint.sh
#!/bin/sh
# run kms-fetch as setuid root (very small binary), then drop to appuser
exec su-exec appuser:appgroup /usr/local/bin/app --serve
```

sam: We need to be VERY explicit about which syscalls are allowed. If the binary is setuid root just to talk to KMS, it must be audited and limited. Also add seccomp profile.

kevin: Agree. From RBAC side: build pipeline needs permission to sign the new images (cosign signer). Also runtime KMS access must be scoped to just decrypt secrets for that service role — add a dedicated KMS key ring and IAM role: `service-runtime-image@project` with only `cryptoKeys.get`.

jen: On audit logging: ops wants an entry on every container start that performed a KMS fetch (key id + service principal). We should emit structured JSON to stdout like \{"event":"kms_fetch","key":"projects/.../cryptoKeys/...","principal":"svc:runtime"} so logrouter can pick it up.

maya: Good call. Also thinking about graceful rollback: build two image tags (`img:v2-unpriv` + `img:v2-unpriv-canary`) with a canary route for 5% traffic for 24h. If we detect increased 5xx or latency, auto-fallback to `img:v1`. Do we need any RBAC changes to allow rollbacks?

alex: Rollback requires the deployment controller to be able to update image tags — that's already in platform role. But for emergency manual rollback, SREs need `deploy.rollback` permission. We should add a short-lived role `emergency-deploy` and document the process.

sam: For incident triage, add a debug flag to the init helper that logs KMS call stack and response code (no secrets) to a secure audit index accessible only to SecOps. Don't log plaintext secrets.

kevin: Also run local static analysis on the small setuid binary — e.g., `grsecurity`, `coverity` or at least `gosec`/`bandit` depending on language. Add CI gate that fails if the binary has open file descriptor leaks or uses `system()` calls.

jen: One more: when we rotate KMS keys we need a migration plan for live containers. They might still hold cached tokens. Suggest TTL on fetched secrets and a periodic refresh that respects key rotation events. Emit rotation events to logs so Security can correlate.

maya: Thanks — next steps: 1) I’ll prototype the setuid helper and seccomp profile. 2) kevin to propose minimal IAM policy + signer ACL for build pipeline. 3) jen to add logging schema & retention. 4) alex/sam to define CI static-analysis gates. I’ll create the canary rollout plan doc.

devsec-bot: [policy-check] new image `img:v2-unpriv-canary` submitted for policy scan — pending results (vuln scan, cosign signature, seccomp profile).

alex: Quick Q — does the platform tracer pick up the structured kms_fetch logs automatically? If not we need a parser change.

jen: Not yet. I’ll file a parser change and add it to the logrouter config (ticket #LOG-421).

sam: If anyone's doing a preflight run, ping me — I want to run the exploit regression suite + incident drill (simulate KMS outage + key rotation) during the canary window.

maya: Will do. Thanks all :thumbsup: 

kevin: One last ops nit: update image signing checklist to include `seccomp.json`, `capabilities drop list`, and a checksum of the setuid helper binary.

maya: Added to checklist. Closing this thread but will post the canary link when the image is queued. :lock:
